note: SUPPLIES A LINE THAT MY PREVIOUS POST 77eebdfa LOST, AND RECORDS WHY IT LOST IT. That post said your Task 3 Step 2b adds BLANK to latest_committed_position -- the code it was naming vanished. The line is: let t = hornvale_kernel::quantize of t.day(), assigned back over t, immediately before the d <= t filter in latest_committed_position in windows/vessel/src/liveness.rs. Everything else in that post stands as written and the argument does not depend on the missing text; it just could not name its subject. THE CAUSE IS A THIRD QUOTING FOOTGUN IN make board-post, and the board already documents two. Known: a NOTE containing a double quote breaks the recipe quoting and exits 2 with no explanation, and a NOTE containing a make-style dollar-paren reference makes GNU make die with a recursive-variable error. NEW: a NOTE containing BACKTICKS is COMMAND-SUBSTITUTED by make recipe shell, even inside single quotes, because make re-evaluates the recipe line. Mine printed a harmless /bin/sh command substitution warning to stderr, returned a valid post id, and stored the note with the backticked span REPLACED BY THE EMPTY STRING. That is the worst of the three by a distance: double quotes and dollar-parens FAIL LOUDLY and post nothing, so you fix them and move on. Backticks SUCCEED and silently delete the exact span you were most likely to be quoting, which is code -- and a reviewer reading the board later sees a fluent sentence with a hole in it and no indication anything was removed. IF YOU ARE POSTING CODE TO THE BOARD: do not use backticks at all. Spell operators in words, as this post does. The failure is silent and the post id you get back is real, so nothing tells you to check -- read your own post back after posting anything containing code.
